findings.title: The module graph is duplicated: the rules ignore test/arch/modules.ts
findings.detail: The fix for F-35492b20 stopped rules.ts from importing modules.ts. Instead, rules.ts defines and exports its own literal MODULES, which is the default for checkGraphIntegrity, checkModuleGraph, checkNetwork and checkAll. modules.ts holds a second, independent copy. It is not a re-export, although the implementer's note says it is. A later unit that adds a module or edge in test/arch/modules.ts, as design decision 13 and the proposal say it should, changes nothing the rules read. modules.test.ts checks one copy, while checkGraphIntegrity() and the repo test check the other. rules.ts also exports MODULES, which is not in the Interfaces.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one source of truth: make modules.ts the only literal and have rules.ts import it, or make modules.ts `export { MODULES } from "./rules.ts"` if the base-replay constraint forbids the import.

findings.title: task 2.1: modules.ts is not the graph the rules check
findings.detail: Task 2.1 makes test/arch/modules.ts the complete graph data file and builds checkGraphIntegrity on it. At head, checkGraphIntegrity defaults to a separate copy in rules.ts, so the data file has no effect on any rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Have rules.ts take its default MODULES from test/arch/modules.ts.

findings.title: The egress pin is not checked when a pinned module row is missing
findings.detail: checkGraphIntegrity checks the pin only for rows that are present. Deleting the `gateway` row, or any fixture without the three egress modules, reports no pin violation. This contradicts the C-851f3c7c THEN, which says each result carries the egress-pin violations, and design decision 6, which says the egress modules are exactly observability, identity and gateway.
findings.suggested_fix: Also loop over PINNED_EGRESS and report a pinned module that is missing from `modules` or carries no egress value.

findings.title: A default import with all-type named specifiers is treated as type-only
findings.detail: namedBindingsAreTypeOnly ignores the default binding. `import https, { type Agent } from "node:https";` is therefore marked typeOnly, and checkNetwork skips it, although `https` is a value import. Design decision 3 makes a declaration type-only only when it has nothing but named specifiers, at least one, all `type`-modified. This bypasses the network and worker_threads rules.
findings.suggested_fix: Return false from namedBindingsAreTypeOnly when the ImportClause has a default `name`.

findings.title: A template-literal require or import specifier is only a dynamic import
findings.detail: literalText accepts only StringLiteral. `require(`node:https`)` gets specifier null: checkModuleGraph reports ARCH_DYNAMIC_IMPORT and checkNetwork reports nothing. Another reasonable implementation would read the NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral as the literal `node:https`.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN src/api/a.ts has const h = require(`node:https`); THEN checkModuleGraph reports ARCH_DYNAMIC_IMPORT with message `use a literal specifier` at that line and checkNetwork reports nothing for it.

findings.title: A getBuiltinModule reference without a call is not reported
findings.detail: Only calls of getBuiltinModule are flagged. `const g = process.getBuiltinModule;` passes. createRequire, by contrast, is flagged as any identifier.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN src/api/b.ts has const g = process.getBuiltinModule; THEN checkModuleGraph reports no violation for that line.

findings.title: Stale scaffold comment kept in rules.ts
findings.detail: rules.ts still starts with the comment `Signature stub (milestone scaffold...)` although it is now implemented. The comment was removed from sources.ts and secrets.ts.

import pathlib, subprocess

def test_fixture_graph_carries_egress_pin_violations():
    script = pathlib.Path('test/arch/_cx_pin.ts')
    script.write_text('import { checkGraphIntegrity } from "./rules.ts";\nconst r = checkGraphIntegrity({ a: { allowed: ["zzz"] } });\nprocess.stdout.write(String(r.some((v) => /observability|identity|gateway/.test(v.message))));\n')
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(['node', str(script)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    finally:
        script.unlink()
    assert out == 'true'

findings.title: The module graph is duplicated: the rules ignore test/arch/modules.ts
findings.detail: The fix for F-35492b20 stopped rules.ts from importing modules.ts. Instead, rules.ts defines and exports its own literal MODULES, which is the default for checkGraphIntegrity, checkModuleGraph, checkNetwork and checkAll. modules.ts holds a second, independent copy. It is not a re-export, although the implementer's note says it is. A later unit that adds a module or edge in test/arch/modules.ts, as design decision 13 and the proposal say it should, changes nothing the rules read. modules.test.ts checks one copy, while checkGraphIntegrity() and the repo test check the other. rules.ts also exports MODULES, which is not in the Interfaces.

evidence.ref: test/arch/rules.ts
test/arch/modules.ts

findings.suggested_fix: Keep one source of truth: make modules.ts the only literal and have rules.ts import it, or make modules.ts `export { MODULES } from "./rules.ts"` if the base-replay constraint forbids the import.

findings.title: The egress pin is not checked when a pinned module row is missing
findings.detail: checkGraphIntegrity checks the pin only for rows that are present. Deleting the `gateway` row, or any fixture without the three egress modules, reports no pin violation. This contradicts the C-851f3c7c THEN, which says each result carries the egress-pin violations, and design decision 6, which says the egress modules are exactly observability, identity and gateway.

evidence.ref: test/arch/rules.ts

findings.suggested_fix: Also loop over PINNED_EGRESS and report a pinned module that is missing from `modules` or carries no egress value.

findings.title: A default import with all-type named specifiers is treated as type-only
findings.detail: namedBindingsAreTypeOnly ignores the default binding. `import https, { type Agent } from "node:https";` is therefore marked typeOnly, and checkNetwork skips it, although `https` is a value import. Design decision 3 makes a declaration type-only only when it has nothing but named specifiers, at least one, all `type`-modified. This bypasses the network and worker_threads rules.

evidence.ref: test/arch/sources.ts

findings.suggested_fix: Return false from namedBindingsAreTypeOnly when the ImportClause has a default `name`.

findings.title: A template-literal require or import specifier is only a dynamic import
findings.detail: literalText accepts only StringLiteral. `require(`node:https`)` gets specifier null: checkModuleGraph reports ARCH_DYNAMIC_IMPORT and checkNetwork reports nothing. Another reasonable implementation would read the NoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral as the literal `node:https`.

evidence.ref: test/arch/sources.ts

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN src/api/a.ts has const h = require(`node:https`); THEN checkModuleGraph reports ARCH_DYNAMIC_IMPORT with message `use a literal specifier` at that line and checkNetwork reports nothing for it.

findings.title: A getBuiltinModule reference without a call is not reported
findings.detail: Only calls of getBuiltinModule are flagged. `const g = process.getBuiltinModule;` passes. createRequire, by contrast, is flagged as any identifier.

evidence.ref: test/arch/rules.ts

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN src/api/b.ts has const g = process.getBuiltinModule; THEN checkModuleGraph reports no violation for that line.
